segment.source: Why did you join the Free Drones?<end>

I... I used to live in North Underrail with my family. Even though it seems like ancient history to me, it's been only four or five years ago. Time flies. I don't know if you have ever been there, $(#chief/sister), but it's the heart - the engine of the Protectorate machinery. Everything is... was a bit more civilized in contrast to what is here, but the Cans are slowly working toward equalizing it. Take that statement as you will.<end>

The facts, however, are that one day they "decided" that my family was helping the "anarchists" and "rebels" and simply took them away. I managed to evade capture somehow and heck, I ended up joining those "anarchists" my family and I were accused of being a part of. The irony. After finding out my family was executed for "collaborating with an anarchist movement," I relocated to South Underrail. It was too much for me. I had to get out of there, I had to.<end>

And here I am, feeding the freedom fighters. ::She smiles.:: I'm a great cook, that's what I hear, and I also heard that I'm a great listener too. Don't know. Hungry mouths aren't picky, that I'm sure. About the second, again, don't know if that's also true. At the end of the day, what I'm doing here isn't so bad. I might not be a fighter, but heck, someone needs to feed those who are. I'm pleased.<end>

The Cans are like a... a cliche totalitarian regime, like a story that offers no surprises, no excitement, a chore to read but for some reason you are forced to do it. Lurkers are equally predictable, in a way, but also unpredictable, if that makes sense. You know they are there, but you don't know exactly where. And you know what they want to do, and you hope they don't catch... you.<end>

Ignore that last comment.<end>

segment.source: What can you tell me about Kokoschka?<end>

Yerslovekzdinianschnik Slavorad Kokoschka. Bam, nailed it. ::She smiles.:: I've been practicing saying his name for months. He was ecstatic when I pronounced it right the first time.
Ah, I remember meeting him for the very first time, I immediately thought, he's a living foreigner cliche. Odd customs, child-like fascination with things new to him here, ancient opinions... He told me that, "He surprised women here talk even when not allowed. Ehehe."<end>

So, you met Corben? Nice, he's one of the Free Drone leaders, together with Alvin Bate. Let me tell you, Trenton is a great strategist: He can sit down, meticulously study maps and Protectorate movement for days until he produces a perfect plan. It's like, you don't see him for a while, on several occasions worrying us if he was alright, but then he shows himself and, heck, you know he came up with something good.<end>

::Your approach prompts the woman to pull out the almost completely burned cigarette out of her mouth and smile. It is a good-natured smile alright, but a somewhat lifeless one: It appears weighted down, fatigued. After a swift movement of her yellowish fingers, one of which is missing its nail, the cigarette is placed back into her mouth, lighting up one final time. Smoke escapes her nostrils and mouth, graying the air between you, after which she puts the cigarette out, pressing it a few times against the ashtray before its glow finally dies.::
Look who decided to pay us a visit. I'm Julia Darling, pleasure to meet ya, $(#chief/sister). You hungry? Thirsty?<end>
